Calibration log: design

Source: calibration-log-design.md

Status: agreed design, 2026-11-01. This records the decisions taken before the code was written; the reference documentation describes the code as built.

Purpose

Manual calibration is judgement. A calibration can be defended later only if the record of that judgement cannot be quietly rewritten. The calibration log is therefore two things at once:

  • an audit trail: append-only, attributed, tamper-evident, and reproducible; and
  • a working record: quick to write, with free-text reasoning as a first-class field, and a readable report generated from it.

A separate, opt-in run log records every model run, calibrated or not, so that the parameter set behind any operational result can be traced to the calibration that produced it.

Decisions

# Question Decision
1 Audit trail or notebook Both: an append-only record with notes and a generated report
2 Storage A project folder of plain YAML files; no database
3 Events Ten entry types, below
4 Identity Declared name and role, stamped with the operating-system login; a Steward cannot sign off their own work
5 Scoring A fixed project scorecard set at data registration; every trial scored on every metric
6 Data Copied into the project by default (copy = FALSE references by path and checksum)
7 Simulated series Checksums for every run; full series kept for candidate, validation and sign-off
8 Report Self-contained HTML built with base R, plus Markdown
9 Interface R functions, with a Shiny app over the same functions covering every action
10 Run log Opt-in, through an option or environment variable
11 Approval Runs flagged as approved, unapproved or superseded; never blocked
12 Delivery Five phases: core, report, run log, app, article

Roles

Roles follow the Owner, Steward and Custodian taxonomy of the F&W governance framework.

Role Acts in the log
Custodian Starts the project, registers data, selects the structure, runs trials and automatic calibrations, writes notes, proposes a candidate, validates it
Steward Signs off and reopens
Delegated Steward As Steward; the entry records the delegation
Owner Named in project_start as accountable; takes no action in the log

A Steward or Delegated Steward may not sign off a project in which they wrote a trial, automatic calibration, candidate or validation entry. Names and logins are both compared, ignoring case and surrounding spaces. The package refuses a self-sign-off.

Identity

Each person declares a name and role once, through options(pdmS7.user = , pdmS7.role = ) or the environment variables PDMS7_USER and PDMS7_ROLE. Every entry records the declared name, the role and Sys.info()[["user"]]. This is an honour system; a mismatch between name and login is visible in the report. A platform identity can later replace the declared name without changing the format.

Project folder

<project>/
  pdms7-project.yml        format version and project identifier; written once
  entries/
    0001-project_start.yml
    0002-data_registered.yml
    0003-structure_selected.yml
    0004-trial.yml
    ...
  data/
    0002/forcing.csv       copies made at registration (unless copy = FALSE)
    0002/observed.csv
  series/
    0009.csv               simulated and observed flow for candidate and validation
  report/                  generated; never edited by hand

Entries are numbered in the order written and are never edited or deleted. A lock directory (entries/.lock, created atomically) serialises writers, so two people can work in one project on a shared drive.

Entry schema

Every entry carries:

Field Content
format Entry format version, currently 1
id Four-digit sequence, the same as the file name prefix
type One of the ten types
timestamp UTC, ISO 8601
author name, role, login
software pdmS7 version, R version, platform, engine
previous MD5 of the previous entry file, or none for the first

Then, by type:

Type Further fields
project_start project: identifier, catchment, gauge, purpose, area_km2, owner, steward, description
data_registered Each series’ source path, stored path, MD5 and summary (rows, period, step, missing values, longest gap); scorecard: warm-up, calibration and validation windows, metrics, headline, log offset, soil fraction
structure_selected Full configuration; reasoning
trial Parent entry; changes from the parent; full configuration; calibration scores; output MD5; verdict (better, worse, inconclusive); reasoning
auto_calibration Parent; bounds; objective; starts; seed; control; the start table; resulting configuration; calibration scores; output MD5; reasoning
note Text; optional entry it refers to
candidate The trial or calibration entry proposed; reasoning; calibration scores; series file and its MD5
validation The candidate; validation scores, alongside calibration scores; series file and MD5; reasoning
test The validated candidate; test scores beside the calibration and validation scores; series file and MD5; reasoning
sign_off The candidate and validation; final configuration; capacity (steward or delegated steward); review checklist; statement
reopen Reason

After sign_off the project is closed. Only reopen may follow; a reopened project accepts entries again, and a later sign-off supersedes the earlier one.

Integrity

  • Chain. Each entry stores the MD5 of the file before it. Checksums of entries, data and series ignore carriage returns, so a Windows checkout that converts line endings does not break the chain. verify_project() recomputes the chain and reports any gap, insertion or alteration. Alteration of the newest entry is caught by the next entry, by a sign-off, or by version control.
  • Data. Every run first checks the registered files against their MD5s.
  • Outputs. Every run records the MD5 of its simulated flow, rounded to 10 significant figures so that last-digit differences between R versions do not register. verify_project(rerun = TRUE) reruns every entry and compares; a mismatch names what has changed in the software since the entry was written.
  • Numbers. Parameters are written with the fewest digits that reproduce the double exactly, so a configuration read back from the log is the configuration that was run.

Scorecard

Scores are fixed when data are registered and computed for every run: NSE, log NSE, KGE and its three components (correlation, variability ratio, mean ratio), RMSE, log RMSE, absolute and signed volume error, peak error, and the three flow-duration-curve signatures of Yilmaz et al. (2008): high-flow volume bias (exceedance below 2 per cent), mid-segment slope bias (20 to 70 per cent) and low-flow volume bias (above 70 per cent). One metric is named the headline, NSE by default, for sorting and charts. The verdict on a trial is the person’s own.

Trials and automatic calibrations are scored on the calibration window only. The validation window is scored once, by the validation entry, so that it stays an honest test.

Every run simulates continuously from the first registered row from initial_state(model, soil_fraction); rows before the calibration window are the warm-up.

Threshold scores

Agreed 2026-11-01, after phases 1 to 5.

# Question Decision
13 What is an event An episode above the threshold; exceedances closer than a minimum gap merge; a simulated crossing within a timing tolerance of an observed one is a hit, matched one to one, closest first
14 Threshold units Flow (m3/s) or level (m), per threshold; levels convert through a registered rating table, interpolated in log flow, never extrapolated
15 Matching settings One set per registration: tolerance 6 h, gap 24 h, minimum duration 0 by default. Event scores need no correct negatives; the chance-corrected scores (POFD, ETS, PSS) are step-based only
16 Weight in calibration A threshold score may be the headline. Automatic calibration may add a weighted threshold term to a continuous objective, using derivative-free Nelder-Mead, since event counts change in steps

Threshold scores join each run’s scores as metric:threshold, for example csi:Flood Warning, so they are logged, verified, reported and ranked like any other.

Structure comparison and the test window

Agreed 2026-11-01.

# Question Decision
17 Which structures A list to choose from; by default the standard PDM and seven one-change variants
18 Parameters and bounds A shipped bounds table per component, with overrides and exclusions; log-scale search for parameters spanning orders of magnitude
19 Ranking On the validation window, with the calibration score and the change shown; optional two-way cross-validation
20 Final check An optional test window, scored once by a test entry (the eleventh type) after every choice; required before sign-off when registered; a poor result does not block sign-off

Each compared structure is logged as ordinary structure_selected and auto_calibration entries sharing a comparison id, so no further entry type is needed and the ranking can be rebuilt from the log. Structures are fitted in parallel workers that write nothing; the entries are written afterwards, in order, by the session that started the comparison.

Run log and register

With options(pdmS7.run_log = ) or PDMS7_RUN_LOG set, run_pdm() appends one CSV row per call under a lock. Each row carries the model’s fingerprint, an MD5 of its canonical components and parameters, so a model built in code and the signed-off YAML match. A register (pdmS7.register or PDMS7_REGISTER) is a YAML file listing project folders, or the folders themselves; its sign-offs are re-read at most once a minute. Calibration evaluations, spin-up cycles and the calibration log’s own reruns are not logged.

Delivery

  1. Project log core, scorecard and integrity checks.
  2. Report: HTML and Markdown, with hydrographs, flow-duration curves, trial tree, progress chart and optional parameter sensitivity.
  3. Run log and approval register.
  4. Shiny app: setup, trials, history, report and sign-off. Shiny is a suggested package only.
  5. Website article: logging a manual calibration.

A pull request follows phase 2 and another follows phase 4.
